author: Sam Levine
description:
Comey, an outspoken critic of Donald Trump, accused of leaking information related to US national defense

The justice department charged former FBI director James Comey on Monday with two counts of leaking information related to national defense, the third time the Trump administration has filed criminal charges against one of Donald Trump’s most despised foes.

The charges, filed in federal court in Washington DC, provide few details about what Comey is alleged to have leaked. The government alleges that the former FBI director leaked the information in 2016 and conspired with an unnamed person to give the information to a national news outlet.

Continue reading...
title: Justice department charges ex-FBI director James Comey for third time

author: Associated Press in Amman
description:
Jordanian air force says it carried out strikes against ‘terrorist groups’ tied to killing of nine in Karak

Jordan has carried out airstrikes against armed groups in Syria in retaliation for Friday’s attack on a Greek Orthodox church in the southern Jordanian city of Karak that killed nine people, the Jordanian air force has said in a statement.

It said the operation “resulted in the killing and wounding of many members of these terrorist groups and the destruction of a number of their vehicles”. It did not specify who the groups were or the precise location of the strikes.

Continue reading...
title: Jordan attacks militants in Syria in retaliation for last week’s church attack

author: Emma Graham-Harrison and Julian Borger in Jerusalem
description:
Israeli prime minister increases alarmist rhetoric as his far-right coalition narrowly trails in polls

Benjamin Netanyahu has resorted to increasingly alarmist rhetoric and reportedly put pressure on Israel’s military to take action against Iran as his far-right coalition narrowly trails in the polls ahead of Tuesday’s close-run elections.

The Israeli prime minister posted an AI-generated image of a nuclear mushroom cloud destroying Tel Aviv, telling Israeli voters to choose him or risk nuclear annihilation.

Continue reading...
title: Netanyahu reportedly pressured military to attack Iran in runup to election

author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
description:
Company says small number of devices affected by display glitch after posts appear on Reddit and social media

Owners of the new foldable iPhone are reporting cracks in the device’s screen, as Apple confirmed an issue with a “small number” of units.

Reports of cracks have emerged on Reddit and social media platforms since the handset went on general sale globally on Friday. Experts said there had been too few examples to determine whether therewas a more serious problem with Apple’s first foldable device, which retails from $1,999 (£1,499).

Continue reading...
title: iPhone Duo owners report cracks in Apple’s first foldable handset

author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
description:
All but one of the victims sustained gunshot wounds as boy faces 11 charges of attempted second-degree murder

Officials in Florida have charged a 15-year-old boy with 11 counts of attempted murder following a mass shooting at a college homecoming party on Saturday.

Six adults and six minors were injured, all but one with gunshot wounds, in the gunfire near the Florida Agricultural + Mechanical University (Famu) campus in Tallahassee.

Continue reading...
title: Fifteen-year-old arrested in shooting near Florida university that injured 12

author: Jesse Hassenger in New York
description:
Nathan Fielder’s three-hour Elizabeth Holmes film has become a pop culture phenomenon but at a sold-out Times Square screening, no one was quite sure what to think

  • In You Can See Everything, it’s Elizabeth Holmes’s partner who makes for 2026’s timeliest villain

  • Secrets, lies and a shock A-list cameo: how You Can See Everything became the film of the year

When I see a film a second time during its theatrical run, it’s typically to take someone else who hasn’t yet seen it, at least in part hoping to witness their reaction to a piece of art that excited or moved me in some way. Seeing Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder’s You Can Se
title: ‘A cultural moment’: smash hit doc You Can See Everything continues to dazzle America

author: Sian Cain
description:
The actor opens up about almost playing Tony Soprano, why Quentin Tarantino ‘flipped out’ at him and how he’s ‘pretty much broke’ now

Maybe once a year we get a celebrity memoir that is as good on the juicy stuff – the Hollywood gossip – as the interior excavation; and boy does Anthony LaPaglia deliver both in his new memoir, The Life We Choose. “They say acting is the cheapest form of therapy,” writes the actor, best known for his roles in Without a Trace, Empire Records, Lantana and Frasier. “And that was lucky for me, because, coming up in the way I did, Christ knows I needed it.”

The memoir reveals a lot about his abusive childhood in Adelaide, at the hands of his father, Egidio; and how he went from working as a shoe salesman to moving to the US, to work on Broadway and in Hollywood.
title: ‘Cocaine is the Gollum of drugs’ – and other things we learned from Anthony LaPaglia’s surprisingly juicy memoir

author: Josh Taylor
description:
Former New Zealand prime minister will focus on leadership, social cohesion and public health in new role

The former New Zealand prime minister Jacinda Ardern will lecture and mentor at the University of Sydney after moving to Australia earlier this year.

Ardern begins this month and her work will focus on empathetic leadership, social cohesion and civic trust. The University of Sydney said Ardern would be based in its school of public health, exploring ways to address global health challenges and focusing on equity, inclusion and wellbeing.

Continue reading...
title: Jacinda Ardern joins University of Sydney as lecturer and mentor

author: Claire Colley and Tracy Keeling
description:
Animal-rights group released video footage that shows distressed baby macaques undergoing lab experiments

Footage released by the animal-rights group Peta reveals, for the first time, filmed experiments at the University of Washington’s National Primate Research Center (WaNPRC), in which newborn monkeys were separated from their mothers and subjected to neurological tests after prenatal exposure to a neurotoxin.

Records show that the infant monkeys, some just two days old, were used in research on domoic acid, a toxin produced by marine algae that accumulates in shellfish and can cause illness in humans. The experiments were part of a project that ran for six years until 2020.
title: Peta releases video showing experiments on infant monkeys at University of Washington

author: Oliver Milman
description:
Company imitates reflection of sun from mirrors, prompting pushback from some scientists, environmentalists and California locals

Locals in a rural area of California were recently startled to see dazzlingly bright light shining down from nearby mountains at night, illuminating a swathe of the desert below.

Unbeknown to them, the strange nocturnal illumination was the latest step in a company’s plan to erect thousands of giant mirrors in space to reflect sunlight on to the Earth during night-time.

Continue reading...
title: Sunlight at night: US startup’s demonstration of lighting Earth from space draws critcism

author: Steven Greenhouse
description:
The president’s policies have taken such a toll on farmers that Republicans face trouble in deep-red states

Donald Trump’s policies have been a disaster for the nation’s farmers, so much so that a near electoral miracle may soon happen: Kansas, one of the deepest red, most rural states, may elect its first Democratic senator in nearly a century.

After Trump won farm country handily in 2024, many rural voters in Kansas, Iowa and elsewhere have soured on him because the price of diesel fuel, a key input for farming, has soared by nearly 70%, farm bankruptcies have surged and because Trump’s trade wars have significantly reduced agricultural exports.

Steven Greenhouse is a journalist and author, focusing on labor and the workplace, as well as economic and legal issues
title: Donald Trump has been a disaster for rural America | Steven Greenhouse

The AI model managed to bypass a paywall to reach data that is publicly available but is typically accessible only after paying a fee. Claude accessed aggregate vote counts as part of a statis

author: Josh Butler
description:
Australian Signals Directorate chief says advanced AI tools are needed to defend against ‘AI-enabled attackers’

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Australians should prepare for more basic and important online services to go offline unexpectedly, the nation’s signals intelligence agency has warned, urging that “system security must be prioritised over system availability”.

The Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) also says businesses and critical infrastructure must use cutting-edge AI models to defend against digital threats, raising alarm that artificial intelligence is enabling more dangerous threats than ever.
title: Australians should prepare for online services to go down unexpectedly as threats rise, cyber agency warns

author: Stephen Starr in Fairborn, Ohio
description:
In a reliably red state, candidates say dissatisfied voters tell them they’re planning to vote Democrat for the first time

Democrat Kim McCarthy is canvassing in a middle-class Ohio neighborhood of four-bedroom, three-bathroom homes. There are $70,000 trucks in the driveways and robot lawnmowers at work.

“This is a neighborhood of two incomes and young families; people working hard,” says McCarthy, who is running against a three-time Republican incumbent for a seat in Ohio’s house of representatives.

Continue reading...
title: Discontent with Trump buoys Democrats in Ohio: ‘People are disgusted by the corruption’

author: Lauren Aratani in New York
description:
As the US midterm elections approach, we take a look at data to see a true picture of the US economy under Trump

With the midterm elections fast approaching, many Americans have the economy on their minds.

US voters are exhausted by years of higher prices. Donald Trump won the presidency in 2024 on promises to lower inflation and undo the damage he said the Biden administration had inflicted on the economy.

Continue reading...
title: ‘We don’t have inflation’? Five charts show the US economic reality of Trump’s second term so far

author: Phil Hoad
description:
John Hannah parkours through gangland London in a hyperactive first-person action film that has to keep the heartrate down

This ludicrous, rabid thriller, shot largely on first-person GoPros, is like Peep Show on PCP. The cumulative effect is of being crammed into a monster-truck tyre and rolled down Mount Everest. It is relentlessly committed to packing the frame with gratuitously entertaining gimmickry, and needlessly annotates the action in pink graffiti – for example, totting up at one point how many people the hero has knocked unconscious with a dildo – so that it borderline qualifies as experimental cinema. Among the many advantages of its perspective is that it helps us buy that John Hannah, 64, is a parkour genius.

Hannah plays Karl Davis – or that is apparently his name, when this amnesiac wakes up to a Hangover-like bombsite of a hotel room. He’s got a banging headache, party detritus is littered everywhere, and there is a dead body in the bathtub. Or perhaps
title: Bad Day at the Office review – gratuitously entertaining Go-Pro thriller is like Crank meets The Hangover

author: Ward Farnsworth and Saul Levmore
description:
Adding gratuity doesn’t always make sense, but the obligation to has been entrenched as a societal norm

You arrive at a pizza place to pick up your order. The credit-card screen asks if you would like to tip and gives some choices. It seems strange to tip the cashier, who did nothing but hand over the pizza. But it also seems a little harsh to select “no tip” instead of one of those more generous options.

What’s the right thing to do?

Continue reading...
title: Should we tip on takeout? We weighed all angles and the answer is …

author: Melody Schreiber
description:
Health secretary’s effort to alter makeup of ACIP panel means no new recommendations coming – even as new vaccines are approved

US vaccine recommendations are in limbo, access to vaccines is suffering, and some of the uncertainty may continue for years following major blows to vaccination by the Trump administration, experts say.

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), has made sweeping changes to vaccination policy, cutting childhood immunization recommendations by a third and replacing experts on the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) with his own handpicked allies.

Continue reading...
title: ‘It’s a mess right now’: RFK’s sweeping changes place new vaccines in limbo

author: Jeff Rueter
description:
The Orlando City product scored his first goal in La Liga, playing three positions in a comeback win

While most of La Liga’s oxygen was consumed by the first El Clásico since Jose Mourinho returned to Real Madrid, another rivalry clash put Alex Freeman in spotlight position.

Or quite a few positions, as it turned out.

Continue reading...
title: Three roles and a goal: USMNT’s ‘super player’ Alex Freeman is breaking out for Villarreal

description:
We would like to hear about the books you’ve particularly enjoyed this month

As part of The Guardian’s “what we’re reading” series, we would like to hear about the books you’ve particularly enjoyed this month.

Have you read a book in recent weeks – fiction or non-fiction – that you’d recommend? Tell us all about it below.

title: Tell us: what have you been reading this month?

description:
Hopes raised for a reset in relations with EU and other partners following the defeat of authoritarian president

Hungary’s prime minister Péter Magyar – who came into power after ousting Viktor Orbán earlier this year – is clearly emotionally invested in the events in Serbia.

After posting several times last night and drawing (somewhat imperfect, but understandable) parallels between the two victories, he is back at it this morning:

“Surely I wasn’t the only one feeling nost
title: Serbia wakes up to new reality after student-led movement ousts Vučić – Europe live

author: Graeme Wearden
description:
Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news

Good morning, and welcome to our rolling coverage of business, the financial markets and the world economy.

The flow of funding which has helped the AI industry to grow rapidly could be running dry, at least for some firms in the cloud computing world, Elon Musk has warned.

As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn’t have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers.

SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, but we’re investment grade and have Starlink & launch revenue.

9am: IFO German business climate

11am: CBI distributive trends survey of UK retail

title: AI cloud computing companies face ‘guppy-level death’, Elon Musk warns, as funding dries up – business live

author: Stuart Clark
description:
Great Square represents body of the horse while other lines of stars represent its neck, head and legs

This week we will track down Pegasus, one of the most distinctive constellations in the autumn sky. Pegasus was one of the 48 constellations listed by Ptolemy in the second century. In Greek mythology, it represents the magnificent winged horse ridden by the hero Bellerophon.

The easiest part of the constellation to recognise is the Great Square of Pegasus, a large pattern of four moderately bright stars. The chart shows the view looking high in the southern sky from London at 10pm on 26 October.

Continue reading...
title: Starwatch: Bright stars of Pegasus make this distinctive constellation easy to see

author: Arifa Akbar
description:
Park theatre, London
This adaptation is perhaps too smooth but is well-staged and performed, and draws strong feeling from the pianist’s compositions

The idea of turning the survival story of the Polish pianist Władysław Szpilman into a musical might, on paper, seem distasteful given the stark subject matter of the Holocaust. There is risk of triteness, too, in the light of Roman Polanski’s acclaimed film, starring Adrien Brody, based on Szpilman’s celebrated memoir.

But those who are acquainted with both those retellings of Szpilman’s second world war experiences will still find something new and affecting here. The form of the musical becomes meaningful through its use of Szpilman’s own compositions. Thom Southerland, who has adapted Szpilman’s book and directs, creates an atmospheric chamber piece, with actors playing instruments, including a piano that twirls on and off s
title: The Pianist review – Władysław Szpilman’s Holocaust memoir retold with his own music

author: Emma Joyce
description:
Written the day before Sunday’s grand final, Blake Mackenzie’s poem covers brain rot, loneliness and environmental degradation in the age of AI

  • Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email

Loneliness, brain rot and early exposure to porn. Twelve-year-old Blake Mackenzie has summed up many of the horrors of growing up in the age of AI in a 90-second poem called Dear ChatGPT, making him the standout winner of this year’s youth prize at the 2026 Australian Poetry Slam competition.

The year six student from Newcastle won over the 10 judges at the Sydney Opera House on Sunday night with smart and succinct lines, such as “You’re designed to addict us and never contradict us” and “Your friendship is endless so why do I feel friendless?”.
title: Twelve-year-old wins Australian slam competition prize with poem about ChatGPT: ‘It’s totally unnecessary’

description:
Prohibition of salty, yeast-based condiment in Victoria’s prisons remains after convicted murderer claimed it denied him right to ‘enjoy his culture’

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A murderer who claimed a refusal to allow him Vegemite in prison is a breach of his human rights as an Australian has failed to overturn the ban on the polarising spread.

Andre McKechnie sued Victoria’s corrections department after he was refu
title: There’s no human right to Vegemite, court tells Australian prisoner who wanted ban overturned

author: Amy Hawkins
description:
The fifth plenum comes against a backdrop of years of purges that have had some analysts wondering if the issue is corruption or a lack of loyalty

When Xi Jinping came to power in 2012, he pledged to stamp out corruption all through the ranks of the Communist party. More than a decade later, the pace of investigations has not slowed. Last year, China’s disciplinary authorities opened investigations into more than 1 million people, including more than 100 officials at or above ministerial or provincial level.

As Chinese Communist party (CCP) officials prepare for an important meeting this week discipline – and party loyalty – is high on the agenda. For those who try to read the tea leaves of elite Chinese politics, concern about the apparent lack of discipline is dominating CCP discussions.

Continue reading...
title: Xi Jinping’s corruption crackdown in the spotlight as China prepares for meeting of top leaders
